sections.title: Kinds of state

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: Your PDFs do not cover this topic, so this page was written for the site. Your 12-week plan lists React, hooks, rendering, performance, state management and TypeScript. Check it against the official documentation, or give me a PDF to replace it.

blocks: Most state-management pain comes from treating all state alike. Sort it first, and the tool usually chooses itself.

rows: Is this dropdown open, input text

blocks.title: Where should this state live?

sections.title: Context
blocks: Context passes a value to any depth without threading props. It is not a state manager: every consumer re-renders when the value changes, so it suits rarely changing values.

sections.title: useReducer
blocks: When several values change together, a reducer puts every transition in one pure function, which is easy to test without rendering.

sections.title: Server state is different
blocks: Data from your API is a cache of something you do not own: it can go stale and needs loading states, retries and invalidation. Libraries handle this, and most of what people once kept in Redux disappears.

blocks.title: Gotcha
blocks.text: Do not copy props or server data into state. Two copies drift apart. Derive what you can during render, and keep one source of truth.

blocks.title: Interview angle
blocks.text: **When would you use Redux?** Only for complex client state shared widely, with many transitions you want to trace. Most apps need local state, Context for rare globals, and a query library for server data.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Sort state by kind before choosing a tool.
- Server state belongs in a query library.
- Context suits rarely changing values, because all consumers re-render.
- Keep one source of truth, and derive the rest.

items.question: Why is Context a poor fit for a frequently changing value?
items.answer: Every consumer re-renders whenever the value changes, even those using only part of it.

items.question: Where should a search term live if users share links to results?
items.answer: In the URL query string, so a link or a refresh restores it.

items.question: What problem does a query library solve that `useEffect` plus `useState` does not?
items.answer: Caching, deduplicating requests, background refetching, retries and invalidation after mutations.
